terrain: Calm fresh pond water for a cozy pixel art farming RPG, muted blue teal, flat high top-down orthogonal ground, sparse short pale blue ripple strokes, simple compact pixel clusters, low contrast interior, no ocean waves, no rocks or objects, no outlines around individual tiles. -> Soft green grassy pond bank matching farming lawn base #43894f. Grass ground with sparse small leaf strokes, irregular rounded natural grassy shoreline, narrow dark teal submerged edge and subtle lighter shallow water at the shore. Flat bank, no cliff, no stone retaining wall, no square pool coping. Cozy hand-pixelled 16-bit farming game style. No flowers, buildings or objects, no realistic texture, no blur, no dithering.
tiles: 16
tile_size: 16x16px
view: high top-down
style: basic shading, low detail

download_png: https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/tilesets/9564912a-cb14-4dc8-9c51-dd2af746cb6b/image
download_png_inline: https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/tilesets/9564912a-cb14-4dc8-9c51-dd2af746cb6b/image?inline=true  (same PNG served from this host — use it if your egress blocks backblaze.pixellab.ai)
download_metadata: https://api.pixellab.ai/mcp/tilesets/9564912a-cb14-4dc8-9c51-dd2af746cb6b/metadata

placement: pick each tile by its corners (NW/NE/SW/SE) or pattern_4x4, then slice the sheet with that tile's `bounding_box` from the metadata — it is the exact rect, and it is correct for BOTH the 16-tile sheet and the 25-tile transition sheet. The metadata endpoint computes bounding_box when serving (it is not a stored column, so querying the database for it finds nothing) and strips each tile's `image` object, so there is no per-tile URL to fetch. Two things are NOT sheet positions: the `wang_N` NAME, and `original_position` (the generation grid — its row can exceed this sheet). Using either is what produces horizontal banding.
